title: Krein perturbation determinant as Cauchy master of the spectral shift function
expression_sketch: H, H0 self-adjoint, V = H - H0 trace class. Perturbation determinant on rho(H0): D(z) = Det(I + V * (H0 - z)**(-1)). D is holomorphic on rho(H0); D'(z)/D(z) = Tr(R(z) - R0(z)) for z in rho(H) intersect rho(H0). Krein: ln D(z) = Integral(xi(lambda)/(lambda - z), (lambda, -oo, oo)) for Im(z) != 0, with xi(lambda) = (1/pi) * lim_{eps->0+} arg D(lambda + I*eps) for a.e. lambda in R. Trace formula: Tr(f(H) - f(H0)) = Integral(f'(lambda)*xi(lambda), lambda). Resolvent specialisation: Tr((H - z)**(-1) - (H0 - z)**(-1)) = -Integral(xi(lambda)/(lambda - z)**2, lambda) for z in C \ (spec(H0) union spec(H)). Birman-Krein: Det S(lambda; H, H0) = exp(-2*pi*I*xi(lambda)) for a.e. lambda in the absolutely continuous spectrum of H0. Integral xi = Tr(V) and Integral |xi| <= ||V||_1.
latent_structure: The holomorphic perturbation determinant D(z) on rho(H0) is the master object. The spectral shift xi is its real-axis boundary value of arg/log, i.e. a Stieltjes inversion of ln D. Resolvent traces, Lifshitz-Krein traces of f(H)-f(H0), and the scattering phase (Birman-Krein) are members of that one Cauchy/Herglotz family. Not a CSE of two resolvents and not a Lehmann spectral representation of a single Green function.

z.notes: spectral parameter of the perturbation determinant

lambda.notes: real energy at which xi is recovered by a boundary value

function_domains.D: perturbation determinant Det(I + V R0(z)), holomorphic on rho(H0)
function_domains.xi: Krein spectral shift function of the pair (H, H0), in L1(R)
function_domains.S: scattering matrix of the pair (H, H0) on the ac spectrum of H0

nonzero_conditions.statement: D(z) is defined on the resolvent set rho(H0); ln D is taken in C+ / C- with arg D(z) -> 0 as |Im z| -> infinity
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: Yafaev, arXiv:math/0701301, Section 2: D holomorphic on rho(H0); branch of ln D fixed by arg D(z) = 0 as Im z -> infinity

analytic_domains.statement: The perturbation determinant D(z) is holomorphic on the resolvent set rho(H0)
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Yafaev, arXiv:math/0701301, Section 2: 'The function D(z) is holomorphic on rho(H0)'

analytic_domains.statement: ln D(z) = Integral xi(lambda)/(lambda - z) d lambda holds for Im z != 0
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Yafaev, arXiv:math/0701301, Theorem 2.1: ln D(z) = Integral xi(lambda)(lambda - z)**(-1) d lambda, Im z != 0

analytic_domains.statement: Carey-Gesztesy-Levitina-Sukochev restatement: ln(Delta_{H/H0}(z)) = Integral xi(lambda; H, H0)/(lambda - z) d lambda for Im(z) != 0
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Carey, Gesztesy, Levitina, Sukochev, arXiv:1505.04895, Theorem 2.2

analytic_domains.statement: Resolvent trace formula is written for z in C \ (spec(H0) union spec(H))
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Gesztesy-Makarov, arXiv:math/9903186, Theorem 3.6: Tr((H-z)**(-1)-(H0-z)**(-1)) = -Integral xi(lambda)(lambda-z)**(-2) d lambda

branch_conventions: ln D in the half-planes Im z != 0 is the branch with arg D(z) -> 0 as |Im z| -> infinity (Yafaev Section 2).
xi(lambda) = pi**(-1) lim_{eps->0+} arg D(lambda + i eps) for a.e. lambda in R (Krein inversion).
Convention (H0 - z)**(-1) as in Yafaev's D(z) = Det(I + V R0(z)).

limit_domains.statement: For a.e. lambda in R, xi(lambda) = pi**(-1) lim_{eps->0+} arg D(lambda + i eps); the limit exists a.e.
limit_domains.label: DECLARED
limit_domains.source: Yafaev, arXiv:math/0701301, Theorem 2.1; equivalently Carey et al. arXiv:1505.04895 (2.5): xi = pi**(-1) lim_{eps down 0} Im ln Delta(lambda + i eps)

derived_conditions.label: DERIVED

public_source: Yafaev, arXiv:math/0701301, Theorem 2.1 (https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701301); Krein, Mat. Sb. 33 (1953); Carey-Gesztesy-Levitina-Sukochev, arXiv:1505.04895, Theorem 2.2.
why_not_cse_lgg: CSE can share a resolvent difference. LGG antiunifies two traces. The scientific object is a holomorphic Fredholm determinant on rho(H0) whose boundary arg is the spectral shift, reconstructing both the Lifshitz-Krein trace and the scattering phase.
proposer_leak_risk: Do not plant 'Lehmann', 'Krein SSF', or 'perturbation determinant' as gold names in a later proposer view. Keep this distinct from the historical Lehmann master (ac-r05) and from Hilbert first-resolvent identity (ac-r01).
notes: Not Lehmann: that packages G(z) = Integral rho/(z-x) for one Green function. Here the master is ln Det(I + V R0(z)) for a trace-class pair. Not Kato simple eigenvalue. Boundary value of arg D uses a written eps down 0+ inversion (Krein), not folklore i epsilon in a scattering kernel. is_guo=false. Not admitted here.
